Both evaluate temporal progression of germ cell loss (C39, C41-C44) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C40 while peer review does not explicitly address it. Both affirm the timing analysis and histological tracing of the fertility defect to postnatal testis, describing the data as robust.

Both evaluate the homing defect (C45, C48-C50) as SUPPORTED with complete agreement. OpenEval also includes C3 in this group. Both describe the VASA/SOX9 co-staining and FOXO1 data as convincing, with peer reviewers affirming this represents a key mechanistic finding about SSC precursor homing.

Both affirm the AS detection methods and results as robust and convincing, though OpenEval notes functional consequences remain to be validated.

Both address Tial1/Tiar regulation (C66-C73, C7, C92-C93, C96) but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval finds the binding and splicing regulation data convincing, while peer reviewers express mixed views, with one explicitly questioning whether altered Tial1 splicing mediates SRSF1 loss effects.

Perfect alignment on protein interaction data (C74-C78, C8) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. Both accept the IP-MS, Co-IP, and domain mapping data as convincing and well-designed. OpenEval notes that functional significance in vivo requires further demonstration, while peer reviewers describe datasets as useful resources.
